newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to allow locals to invest in ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to allow locals to invest in ADRs.

text.p: Brazilian investors will be allowed to purchase American Depositary Receipts issued by Brazilian companies, the president of Brazil's Securities Exchange Commission said.
Francisco Costa e Silva said the National Monetary Council approved a proposal to scrap a restriction which has prevented Brazilians from trading in ADRs in companies based in Brazil.
The move was taken to give local investors better conditions to compete with international traders, Costa e Silva said.
In the future, the government might relax other restrictions to allow, for example, Brazilian investors to buy shares in foreign companies on international markets, he said.
"For the time being, opening up depositary receipts is sufficient," the exchange head said.
